references.text: Joshua urges the descendants of Joseph to clear the forest in the hill country, which is the context for the promise in verse 18.
Mentions iron chariots as part of the enemy's military strength, the same challenge faced by the descendants of Joseph.
Judah could not drive out those living in the valley because they had iron chariots, the same situation described here.
Sisera had nine hundred iron chariots, showing the Canaanites' military superiority with iron chariots.
Describes Sisera's iron chariots being defeated, demonstrating that God can overcome even such obstacles.
Israel's promise not to fear enemies with horses and chariots, because the Lord is with them.
The Lord promises to drive out the Canaanites, providing the basis for the promise of victory over those with iron chariots.
